issue_paraphrase: Writing an implicit string concatenation that mixes a raw string literal with a regular one trips a false-positive warning: an expression such as a raw escape pattern followed by a normal string inside a list or an assignment is flagged as if a comma had been forgotten. The concatenation is in fact deliberate, because raw and non-raw literals cannot be merged into a single string anyway. The warning should be suppressed whenever the two adjacent literals differ in whether they are raw, but the linter currently reports it regardless.
fix_summary: StringConstantChecker now stores the raw token text alongside the evaluated value for every string token, and a new helper _is_raw_string_token() inspects the token prefix; when adjacent STRING tokens differ in rawness the implicit-str-concat branch is skipped. The functional test gains three mixed raw/non-raw cases (no expected messages).
notes: Fully offline, <1s. The project's own regression signal is the functional test tests/functional/i/implicit/implicit_str_concat.py checked out from the fix commit: run 'python3 -m pytest tests/test_functional.py -k implicit_str_concat -q' (the test ids with 4 passes come from test_functional's parametrization). The oracle can also just diff pylint stdout/exit code on the 2-line repro. The repro must be written into a file (pylint only checks files, not stdin).

issue_paraphrase: Reading a protected member through self.__class__ inside an instance method is reported as a protected-access violation, even though self.__class__ is just another spelling of type(self) and that form is already accepted by the same check. Any method that reads a class attribute through self.__class__ gets a spurious warning and therefore fails a clean lint run, while the identical access written as type(self) passes. The warning should only fire when the member is reached through some other object's class, and that case must keep warning.
fix_summary: class_checker's protected-access visitor now returns early (no warning) when the expression being accessed is '<first method param>.__class__', treating it as equivalent to type(self) via a new _is_self_class_access() helper. The functional test adds an Issue11160 class: self.__class__._attr accesses must be silent, while other.__class__._attr keeps the protected-access message (one new line appended to the .txt).
notes: Fully offline, <1s with the -k selection. The PASS condition is not 'no output': the other.__class__ warning legitimately remains, so an oracle asserting a silent run would be wrong. Best oracle: assert the self.__class__ lines produce no W0212 while line 10 still does, or use the golden functional test which encodes the exact expected message set. The full pylint test suite is large; always select with -k.

issue_paraphrase: A type annotation that subscripts Generator or AsyncGenerator with an empty tuple, such as Generator[()], makes the linter crash with an internal IndexError instead of producing a report, so the whole file fails to be checked. The check that suggests dropping redundant default type arguments assumes a subscript always carries at least one element and reaches past the end of the list on the empty case. Any source file containing such an annotation ends up unusable by the tool, with only a fatal-error notice to show for it.
fix_summary: visit_subscript in pylint/extensions/typing.py now requires node.slice.elts to be non-empty (added 'and node.slice.elts' to the guard) before building the suggested replacement, so an empty tuple subscript skips the check and never reaches elts[0]. The functional test adds Generator[()] / AsyncGenerator[()] cases for both collections.abc and typing aliases.
notes: Fully offline, <1s. The subtlety: the check lives in the typing extension, so the direct CLI repro (and any task instruction) must pass --load-plugins=pylint.extensions.typing (or run the functional test under tests/functional/ext, which loads extensions automatically). On Python 3.12 the .313.txt variant of the golden test is ignored; the base .txt was NOT updated by the fix (the new lines expect no message), which is what makes the golden test fail at parent (crash) and pass at fix. Do not assert 'exit 0 and empty stdout' without the plugin flag, otherwise the check simply never runs.
